coaching.summary: N. is a 31-year-old journeyman pipe fitter, introverted and anxious around women, with one date in about four years and nothing coming from the apps. He wants a partner and confidence. The rep ran a decent discovery, listed the features, quoted $7,200 with financing in the same breath, ran a live credit application including his SSN, and then answered his request for a day or two with 'I already pulled your credit' and 'financing may not be open tomorrow'. He declined and said he felt rushed and pressured.

turning_point.what: He asked for time to think after the financing was approved; the rep answered with credit-already-pulled urgency rather than finding out what he needed to be sure, and he moved to no and then 'rushed' and 'pressured'.
turning_point.quote: Yes. Now, can I take a day or two to think this over?

coaching.issue: When he said $7,200 is a lot, the rep went straight to monthly-payment reframes and 'we all spend $300 a month on something' without taking money off the table and checking belief in the process. His belief had only been 7 or 8 and he had never reached a 9 or 10.
coaching.better: I hear you, and I'm glad you said it. Let's set the money aside for a second. Do you believe this process gets you talking to women without the anxiety and into a relationship?

coaching.issue: When he asked for a day or two the rep used pressure: she had already pulled his credit and the financing might not be there tomorrow. That created the 'rushed' and 'pressured' reaction and answered the think-it-over with a deadline instead of a question.
coaching.better: Taking time to think is completely fine. What specifically do you want to think through: whether this will work for you, or how to make the monthly amount work? Let's figure out how to make this work for you, not whether you should.

coaching.issue: Price was stated, then financing and a request for an amount he could pay today were added in the same breath. No silence after the number, and the payment solution came before any objection existed.
coaching.better: Based on everything you shared about the anxiety, the confidence and wanting a real plan, I recommend the three-month program with weekly one-on-ones with Kimberly. The investment is $7,200.

coaching.issue: The close promised an outcome ('you will a hundred percent reach your goal') and recited the 80 percent and 20 percent statistics, which the playbook forbids. The pitch was also a feature list, not the four pillars tied to what he had tried.

Elly opened correctly (recording, confidentiality) and ran a long, warm discovery, then pitched a three-phase framework and named $7,200. L. said it was about double what she expected; Elly told her there was no cheaper option, then improvised discounts down to the full three months for $3,500 and promised to send an agreement, leaving the call as a follow-up.

turning_point.what: L. asked directly for a cheaper tier and Elly said there was none, even though a sanctioned bi-weekly tier at $3,600 matched her budget; the next 14 minutes were improvised discounts that ended at half price for the full program.
turning_point.quote: So is this the only option that I have for that price or do you guys offer something less?

coaching.issue: When asked whether $7,200 was the only option, she answered 'Yes.' and then invented a series of prices (half the sessions for $3,500, a $1,000 first call, then the full three months for $3,500). The sanctioned tier that fit a $3,500 budget, bi-weekly with Kim for $3,600 over three months, was never mentioned.
coaching.better: There is another option, L.. Kim also works with clients every other week instead of weekly, for the same three months, at $3,600. Based on how ready you are and how careful you want to be with the money, that's the one I'd recommend for you.

coaching.issue: On the first price reaction she asked how the number sat with her and moved straight to ways to break it up, then to Clarity Pay and in-house payments, without taking money off the table and checking that L. believes in the process. Payment structures were offered into a clear price surprise.
coaching.better: L., setting the money aside for a second: do you believe this process would get you to the partner you want? If the answer is yes, then it's not whether you should do it, it's how we make it work.

coaching.issue: After saying results cannot be guaranteed, she quoted placement statistics and told L. that Kim will get her the result. When L. asked what ensures a result, this was the moment to promise process and visible change, not an outcome.
coaching.better: I can't guarantee a result, L., and no honest coach can. What I can promise is a clear process and a straight read from Kim on how you're showing up, and you'll see visible change in how you date within the first few weeks.

coaching.issue: The pitch was a long spiel on a three-phase framework plus a list of coaching features, and the delivery described only weekly 1:1 sessions and email support. Group coaching calls, the education library and the community were never mentioned, and L. had to ask what kind of service it was.
coaching.better: Here's how it works. Alongside your weekly one-on-one with Kim, you get group coaching calls twice a week, the full education library, and the community, so you're supported every day, not just once a week.

coaching.issue: Never asked what L. thinks has been getting in the way, what she has tried, or her weekly dating mechanics. L. said 'I'm really not putting myself out there at all' and the rep moved on, so there was no belief of hers to build the pitch around.

quality.notes: Recording begins at 8:56 (late join). Location is ambiguous: Istanbul, but she says 'In Canada' and the rep assumes PST. CRM Closer Name is blank; rep is Brianna Patterson.

crm.no_close: She kept saying this is just how I make decisions. She lost her last partner to cancer and she is afraid of being vulnerable and saying something that will upset Kim/them not getting along. I challenged her but she wanted 2/3days to think through it. I challenged her again and said she wouldn't be speaking with Kim so how would it help and isolated it to fear. I offered 1k session to speak with Kim so they can go through it but can't offer anything free because we want people who are committed. I sent her link but she was firm about taking time. I'll have to review to see where I could have created more urgency or pre-handled fear more.

coaching.summary: S., 27, calling from Istanbul, is in a stalled situationship with a man who says he cannot commit because of money, wants marriage and a family, and lost an earlier partner to cancer. Brianna ran a strong discovery and a four-pillar pitch, but the scale check came back uncertain and she quoted $14K anyway. S. asked for a trial, Brianna improvised a $1K single session and pushed hard on her need to think it over, and S. ended the call asking for two or three days with nothing paid.

turning_point.what: The prospect named her real condition for buying, a trial first, right after the price, which showed that belief had not been established before the number was given.
turning_point.quote: I would like to at least have a trial and then make a decision if I think that it's worth it, you know?

coaching.issue: The scale check was the right move, but S. did not give a number ('I feel like I can only know once I communicate with her more'). Brianna restated it as 'you think it would work', moved on, and revealed the price within two minutes. Nothing was done about what kept her from a 9 or 10, so the price landed on an unresolved doubt.
coaching.better: That's fair, S.. If you had to put a number on it today, would it be closer to a 6, a 7 or an 8? And what would need to be true for it to feel like a 9 or 10?

coaching.issue: When S. said she was unsure the program would benefit her and wanted a trial, Brianna asked whether she could pay $14,000 this month, offered to split it, then texted Kim and improvised a $1,000 single session. Those are payment and downsell offers made to a belief objection, and the $1K session is not a sanctioned tier.
coaching.better: I hear that you want to be sure it is worth it before committing, and that is reasonable. Setting the money aside, what would you need to see or hear on your first call with Kim to feel confident this is right for you?

coaching.issue: When S. said she needed to think about it, Brianna cited a '99% rate' of people not coming back, reframed her normal decision style as fear and kept pressing for several minutes ('does a version of you take action?'). S. had said clearly that she thinks for a day or two and then follows through.
coaching.better: Of course, take the two or three days. When we speak again, what is the one question you want answered so you can make the decision? I will check in with you on Wednesday morning.

coaching.issue: She opened by promising everything on the call was confidential, then used another client's first name and mental-health details (an extreme-anxiety story) to answer S.'s fear. She also never said the call was being recorded.
coaching.better: That is a normal feeling before a first call with someone new, and it tells me how much this matters to you. Is there anything you would like me to pass on to Kim so she knows how you like to be spoken to?

coaching.issue: Recommended 'tier one' for $14K and six months. In the sanctioned offer tier 1 is $7,200 for 3 months and the $14,000 six-month program is tier 2, so the label left her with a wrong picture of what the entry tier is. The recommendation was tied to her situationship, which is good, but not tied to her own words.
coaching.better: Based on what you told me about wanting clarity on this relationship and a path to marriage, I would recommend working with Kim weekly one-on-one for six months. The investment is $14,000.

exemplary.quote: what do you feel like would happen if we don't do anything right now?
exemplary.why: Direct cost-of-inaction question, followed by a segment-aware 'what does that darkness look like' that got her to name the fear of ending up alone.

exemplary.quote: paint me a picture. Like, if we are talking a year from now, and this situation with, you know, your partner went exactly how you'd want it, what would that look like?
exemplary.why: Reframes a vague answer into a concrete picture a year out, which led to the why-it-matters and the story of her late partner.

exemplary.quote: You've mentioned that you've tried figuring it out on your own. You've talked to friends, even your sister, about it.
exemplary.why: Opens the Honest Read by tying it to what she has already tried, which is exactly what the pillar calls for.
